FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Home and Daily Life flashcards.

A house is a child’s first country, and this set is its phrasebook. Forty-one cards walk the whole home — the rooms and their furniture, the wash-and-get-ready routines, the kitchen verbs, the chores and the toolbox, the mail by the front door, the sounds the house makes when nobody is watching, and the green habits that keep it all running. The cards speak the everyday words of the US, UK and Canada — and where the countries differ (the tap and the faucet, the torch and the flashlight, the trolley and the cart), both words ride along, so every family hears its own home talking.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    The house hunt

    Call a word from the cards — "sink!" "cushion!" "doormat!" — and your child runs to touch the real thing. Every room of your actual home becomes the answer key, and the sprinting burns each word in deep.

  2. 02

    Same home, two words

    The cards quietly carry both flavors of English: tap and faucet, torch and flashlight, wardrobe and closet, trolley and shopping cart. Point and say both — your child picks a favorite, or keeps both like secrets.

  3. 03

    One card, one room

    Stick the bedroom card on the bedroom door, the bathroom card by the sink, the kitchen card on the fridge. The word lives where the thing lives, and reading the room becomes reading the words.

  4. 04

    The tidy-up draw

    The cleaning, storage and laundry cards make a tidy-up team: draw one at random and do that job together for five minutes. The vacuum cleaner card gets requested first, every time.
